title: Kaplan's God
hook: Kaplan pictured God as the power in the world that makes for goodness and fulfillment

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: decide together. Reconstructionist communities talk a practice through and choose it as a group. Did you decide one thing with someone else? This week ran from the early platform through returning, prophetic, worldwide, and an evolving civilization. Today it closes with God. Day one thousand two hundred thirty-two.

On a refrigerator door, a child's drawing in crayon: a giant in the clouds with a long white beard, looking down at a small house with a crooked chimney. Ask the artist who that is, and the answer comes fast. God. Some grown-ups still carry a version of that drawing around inside them, never revised since they were small. One rabbi looked hard at the drawing and asked a different question. Not where God lives, or what God looks like, but what God does in a human life. His name was Mordecai Kaplan, the thinker behind the Reconstructionist movement we met this week, and his answer is today's word.
screen: `A CRAYON GOD ON THE FRIDGE.` → `NEVER REVISED.` → `WHAT DOES GOD DO?`

segments.voice: Kaplan's God. Start with the Torah's own caution about pictures. It forbids carving an image of God. And when Moses asks God's name at the burning bush, the answer in the King James words is: "I AM THAT I AM." Some readers hear the Hebrew as I will be what I will be, a name that will not sit still for a portrait. Next, the tradition's range. The medieval philosopher Maimonides taught that we can say only what God is not, because every positive description falls short. Kabbalists spoke of Ein Sof, the without-end. So Kaplan stepped into an old conversation; he did not start it. Then Kaplan's own picture. He set aside the idea of a God who reaches in from outside nature to work miracles. Instead he described God as the power in the world that makes for salvation, and by salvation he meant goodness and fulfillment in this life: the pull in a person toward honesty, the force that lets a wounded thing heal, the energy that moves people to build fairer lives together. On this view you meet God less as a voice from the sky and more in what happens when people take up Micah's charge "to do justly, and to love mercy." Believing in God, for Kaplan, meant trusting that the world holds that power, and joining it. Last, the answers he drew. Some readers found his picture freeing, a way to keep praying with honest words. Others, in several movements, replied that a power is not someone who hears, and a prayer needs a listener. Reconstructionist Jews today hold a range of views, and not all of them follow Kaplan here. What his idea leaves on the table is a question, not a verdict: what does a picture of God do in the life of the person who holds it?
screen: `NO CARVED IMAGE. I AM THAT I AM.` · `ONLY WHAT GOD IS NOT.` · `THE POWER THAT MAKES FOR GOODNESS.` · `FREEING TO SOME, TOO THIN TO OTHERS.` · then, large: `MANY WAYS TO PICTURE GOD.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: notice how you picture God. Settle, and breathe. Let the word God come to mind, and see what arrives with it. A face, a light, an empty space, a warmth, a doubt, or nothing at all. Don't correct it and don't argue with it. Just notice. Then ask where that picture came from: a book, a teacher, a grandparent, a painting, a hard night. If you pray, you can pray in silence to God as you understand God. If you don't, simply let the picture be there for a while, and then let it go. The bell holds the time.
Kaplan's God. Mordecai Kaplan's picture of God as the power in the world that makes for goodness and fulfillment, one picture among several in Jewish thought. Today's word.
Your line: many ways to picture God. Today, ask one person, gently, how they picture God, and just listen to the answer without fixing it. Day one thousand two hundred thirty-two.

howItsDone: Reconstructionist prayer books and teachers often invite worshippers to bring their own understanding of God to prayer, and Kaplan's idea of God as the power that makes for goodness is one of the views discussed in the movement.

fork.setup: you're Mordecai Kaplan. people tell you they can no longer pray to a giant in the clouds. what do you offer them?
options: a picture of God as the power in the world that makes for goodness.
tell them to keep the old picture and stop asking.
fork.reveal: Kaplan described God as the power that makes for salvation, meaning goodness and fulfillment in this life. some found it freeing; others said a power cannot hear a prayer.

original.note: Hebrew: the name from the burning bush. the King James has I AM THAT I AM; some readers hear I will be what I will be.

trapdoor: what you thought: a rabbi who didn't believe in God.
what it means: Kaplan spoke of God as the power in the world that makes for goodness and fulfillment, not a being outside nature.
what a scholar hears: a theology that asks what belief does in a life, in an old conversation with Exodus 3:14, Maimonides and Ein Sof.
